description: Each media type's rate is the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; list the media types whose rate is above the unweighted mean of all media types' rates, with the rate and how far above it is.

c.request: Which media types (by name, counting only tracks that have a media type) have a bytes-per-millisecond rate higher than the simple average of that rate across all media types? For each, show the media type name, its rate, and how much it exceeds that average, unrounded. Each media type's rate is the mean of its tracks' individual Bytes/Milliseconds ratios; list the media types whose rate is above the unweighted mean of all media types' rates, with the rate and how far above it is.
c.sql: WITH rates AS (SELECT m.Name AS MediaTypeName, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / NULLIF(t.Milliseconds, 0)) AS Rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType m ON m.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(Rate) AS AvgRate FROM rates) SELECT r.MediaTypeName, r.Rate, r.Rate - o.AvgRate AS ExceedsBy FROM rates r CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE r.Rate > o.AvgRate ORDER BY ExceedsBy DESC;

a.request: For each media type (grouped by name, using only tracks that are linked to a media type), compute its byte rate as the average of each track's `Bytes` divided by that track's `Milliseconds` (tracks with no size ignored). Then take the simple average of these rates across all media types. Which media types have a rate above that overall average? For each, give the media type name, its rate, and how far it is above the overall average (rate minus average), without rounding.
a.sql: WITH rates AS (SELECT mt.Name AS MediaTypeName, AVG(t.Bytes * 1.0 / t.Milliseconds) AS Rate FROM Track t JOIN MediaType mt ON mt.MediaTypeId = t.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL GROUP BY mt.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(Rate) AS AvgRate FROM rates) SELECT r.MediaTypeName, r.Rate, r.Rate - o.AvgRate AS DiffFromAvg FROM rates r CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE r.Rate > o.AvgRate;

b.request: For each media type with at least one track, take the mean of its tracks' Bytes/Milliseconds ratios (skipping tracks with NULL Bytes), average those per-type means without weighting, and list the media types whose mean ratio is above that average, with their name, mean ratio, and unrounded difference from the average
b.sql: WITH type_means AS (SELECT mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name AS Name, AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS MeanRatio FROM MediaType mt JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId, mt.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(MeanRatio) AS AvgMean FROM type_means) SELECT tm.Name, tm.MeanRatio, tm.MeanRatio - o.AvgMean AS Difference FROM type_means tm CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE tm.MeanRatio > o.AvgMean;

d.request: Among media types that have at least one track, which ones have a per-media-type rate (the mean of each track's Bytes/Milliseconds ratio) above the unweighted mean of all media types' rates? For each, give the media type name, that rate, and how far it exceeds the unweighted mean, unrounded.
d.sql: WITH rates AS (SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name, AVG(t.Bytes * 1.0 / t.Milliseconds) AS rate FROM MediaType m JOIN Track t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM rates) SELECT r.Name, r.rate, r.rate - o.mean_rate AS excess_over_mean FROM rates r CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE r.rate > o.mean_rate;
